author: WP20
summary: How to read and write CNA's project records (NEXT.md, CHECKLIST.md, AUDIT.md, plans, integration packets, executable ledgers, versions, sharp-runtime's plan database, handoffs). Counts were alpha.1-era (62 plans, NEXT.md head) and are corrected; the glTF known-defect ledger, registry gates and release-gate history were read at TARGET. The site already had the artifact inventory (review-ai-generated-code) and version rules (make-a-release); the practice rules, packet, ledgers and database figures now live on a new practice deep dive.

concepts.section: Project Practice and Durable Task Tracking
concepts.text: CNA's plans, handoffs, audits and ledgers can explain why code exists while being wrong about whether it exists today; durable practice keeps a chain from intent to source, test, artifact and current status.
tokens: an old plan can explain why code exists while being wrong about whether it exists today

concepts.section: Documents have roles, not equal authority
concepts.text: NEXT.md is a session and integration handoff: at TARGET 6,743 lines of dated sections, newest XNA-ENUM-001 (2026-09-20), with eleven topical NEXT*.md files; it is operational history, not a normalised feature statement.
concepts.note: Corrected: the Bible described the alpha.1 head section (2026-08-18 merge).

concepts.section: Documents have roles, not equal authority
concepts.text: CHECKLIST.md defines repeatable port rules (surface from reference assemblies, behaviour from FNA, CNAEXT for extensions, tests or stated host exceptions); it is policy whose compliance must be checked in code and gates.
tokens: Policy; compliance still has to be checked

concepts.section: Documents have roles, not equal authority
concepts.text: AUDIT.md is a large historical class table with dated banner notes above older rows; a new banner does not refresh old rows, so it is a claim corpus, as are pre-modularisation source audits.

Plan files record numbered tasks with rationale, experiments and owner decisions; alpha.1 had 62 plan_*.md at the root and TARGET has 103 in plans/ plus plan/plan_compilation.md; stable IDs such as GLTF-245 and REMED-GFX-188 link commits, tests and comments to decisions.
concepts.note: Corrected the count for TARGET (104 plan files).

target.evidence: git ls-tree at 1bb2145d (62 plan_*.md) and 009d40f5 (104); plans/plan_gltf.md; remediation/REMEDIATION_INDEX.md

concepts.text: A done marker is a claim: check the named path, test, commit and behaviour before quoting a task, and update forward pointers instead of erasing identifiers; CNA's C ABI release gate records an illusory closure (73 rules matching whole headers).
tokens: A done marker is still a claim

concepts.text: Split a task that grows across independent renderers or failure modes; the parent becomes a tracking pointer and each child carries its own acceptance evidence (e.g. CBIND-051A to 051E).
tokens: The parent becomes a tracking pointer

concepts.text: The alpha.1-era renderer-integration campaign record (lane SHAs, merge order from path interaction, signed no-fast-forward merges, recomputed registry arithmetic) is cited as the model integration record.
concepts.note: That campaign integrated an earlier, broader renderer set and was not re-read at TARGET; the page keeps the generic packet and links the site's worked reading of the 009d40f5 head merge instead.

concepts.text: A checkpoint packet for large integrations holds base and input SHAs with no hidden working-tree state, path-overlap and ordering rationale, exact commands with renderer and host, machine-readable results and skips, separated new defects, and a clean-tree check plus next-step handoff.
A prose claim that all lanes passed cannot replace the packet, especially when a lane was only compile-checked or ran under a substitute runtime.

glTF known defects live as tests that pass while CNA is broken and fail on a partial fix; a ledger test checks both directions between the corpus ledger and the tests, and at TARGET the open set is empty with D1-D8 and GLTF-241 remediated.

Registry gates compare derived sets: check_renderer_identities.py compares enum, CMake list, runtime registry and stated document counts; RendererDescriptorGate.cmake compiles every family's descriptor; the WebGPU plan summary is computed from its rows.

General rule: derive any finite set a record names and compare it, checking uniqueness, status vocabulary, set equality, path existence and non-empty parsing, with negative fixtures that prove the validator goes red.
tokens: set equality, path existence and non-empty parsing

concepts.text: Executable documents rot too: validators or build files can keep reading moved inputs or stale prose counts, and a gate that cannot find its input is not evidence; moves must update code, tests, validators and docs together.
tokens: a gate that cannot find its input is not current evidence
concepts.note: The Bible's 'four wired validators' count at its pin was not re-counted at TARGET; the page states the rule with the drift-table examples.

target.evidence: cmake/Tests/ModuleProbes.cmake (stale identity count, per the site's drift table)

concepts.text: Product version authority is the root CMake numeric version plus CNA_VERSION_PRERELEASE, generated into CNA/Version.hpp and exposed through CNA::getVersionString() and CNA_VERSION_* macros.
The experimental C ABI has its own version in CNA/C/abi.h (0.29.0) that moves with ABI changes, not product tags; a release record names both coordinates when the C surface is in scope.
tokens: names both where the C surface is in scope

concepts.text: Pre-1.0 SemVer identifies a state and signals prerelease status without a stable-API promise; task IDs answer why and how, the tag answers which immutable product state.
tokens: a task answers why and how

concepts.text: sharp-runtime's plan.sqlite3 at f827a6c5 has 16,201 task rows (1,082 ported, 14,979 ignored, 140 ignore, 118 out of scope) and 2,183 tickets; at 41b918c9 16,207 tasks (1,087 ported) and 2,417 tickets.
concepts.note: Extended with the site's sharp-runtime pin.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime plan.sqlite3 at f827a6c5 and 41b918c9 (queried with the two SELECTs shown)

concepts.text: The denominator matters: ported rows are counterparts under the schema, not a 6.7% behavioural parity with the whole BCL, and Doxygen @note Status tags are secondary hints that can drift.
Publish the query with the number (SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM task GROUP BY status; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ticket) so later changes are visible.
tokens: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM task GROUP BY status

concepts.text: Keep observations (reproducible), inferences (connected evidence) and decisions (policy) apart so plans do not outlive their premises; CNA's gate record shows an owner decision kept distinct from 'no C form'.

target.evidence: docs/c-api/RELEASE_GATE.md (2026-08-28 owner ruling on CNB rows)

concepts.text: A handoff states what is complete and verified, what remains, read-only repositories, approvals needed, failed approaches and known-stale documents, without growing into a transcript; NEXT.md and AUDIT.md were last changed 194 commits before TARGET.

Authority order when records disagree: current source and generated configuration, then tests and retained artifacts, then accepted integration/remediation records, then plans, audits, READMEs and comments.
tokens: Comments often preserve the best explanation and the worst status
